# SAN-171 — Password reset link generated by the server operator

Owner (2026-10-19): santi has no email yet (SAN-68 waits for a domain). Someone who forgot the
password gets back in through a one-time link the server operator generates and sends by chat.

## Decisions (owner)

| # | Question | Winner |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Who can generate a reset | **The server operator only**, through `santi-server reset-link <email>`. Accounts are global: a project admin who could reset a member could take over an account that also runs other projects. The operator already has the database, so the command adds no new power. No instance-admin role, env list or web button (post-1.0, only if the command becomes a chore). |
| 2 | What generating a link does to the password | **Nothing.** The old password keeps working until the new one is set; nobody is locked out by a link they never open. |
| 3 | Sessions and tokens after the reset | Every session of the account is revoked; the person is signed in on a new session. API tokens stay. |
| 4 | Password rules on the reset page | Today's rules (`auth::domain::check_password`, 10–128 chars). Stronger rules are SAN-174. |

## Link rules

- 32 random bytes, URL-safe; only the SHA-256 hash is stored (same pattern as invite tokens).
- Valid 24 h, single use. Generating a new link for the same account deletes the previous one.
- URL: `<SANTI_PUBLIC_URL or http://localhost:8080>/reset/<token>`.
- Rate limited like invite accept.

## Command

- `reset-link <email>`, a binary next to `bin/seed`, reads `DATABASE_URL` and builds the address
  from `SANTI_PUBLIC_URL`, else `https://$RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN`, else `http://localhost:8080`.
- The production image is distroless (no shell), so the operator runs it from their machine against
  the production database's public URL:
  `DATABASE_URL=<postgres public url> SANTI_PUBLIC_URL=<santi url> cargo run -p santi-server --bin reset-link -- <email>`.
- Known email: prints the URL and when it expires. Unknown email: exits non-zero with
  `no account with that email`. Email compared case-insensitively, like sign-in.

## API

- `GET /api/password-resets/{token}`: 200 `{ email, expires_at }` for a live token; 404 otherwise
  (unknown, used and expired look the same).
- `POST /api/password-resets/{token}` `{ password }`: checks the password rules, replaces the hash
  (Argon2id), deletes the token and every session of the user, opens a new session (cookie like
  login), returns the user. 404 for a dead token, 422 for a weak password. One transaction.
- Both are public (no session). OpenAPI updated.

## Web (`/reset/$token`, public route)

- Live link: title "Choose a new password", the account email read-only, "New password" and
  "Confirm password" (16px fields, show/hide, 44px targets), button "Save and sign in"; mismatch and
  rule errors under the field. Success: lands on the home page signed in.
- Dead link: "This reset link has expired or was already used. Ask the person who sent it for a new
  one." and a link to sign in.
- Loading and network-error states like the join page. 375 px first, light and dark.

## Acceptance

- Command prints a working link for an existing email and fails for an unknown one.
- The link sets a new password and signs in; old sessions stop working; the old password fails.
- A used, expired or wrong token is rejected (API 404, page shows the dead-link state).
- qa review (auth) before merge.
